descricao_original: This tissue, composed of both woven and lamellar compact bone, represents a later stage in bone formation. During bone formation, the first bone produced is woven bone that is gradually remodeled into lamellar bone. As a result, some areas will be composed of both woven and lamellar bone, as seen here. Similar events occur during adult remodeling and repair following a fracture. 600x

marcadores.explicacao_original: In woven (immature) bone, osteocyte lacunae are irregularly arranged within the matrix which lacks lamellae. Lacunae are rounder than are those in mature bone and the matrix has a more bluish tint due to the proteoglycans in the matrix and reduced collagen fiber content. Woven bone is not as strong as lamellar bone.

marcadores.explicacao_original: Lamellar (mature) bone is organized in lamellae with orderly arranged, flattened lacunae between them. This organization gives lamellar bone more strength. In the bone shown here, the lamellae are arranged as cylindrical structures called Haversian systems or osteons with a central Haversian canal. This canal is lined by an endosteum and contains one or more blood vessels. On the surface of bones, lamellae are arranged as flattened plates.
